items.titleEn: Smith hails "hungry" young Gunners
items.summaryEn: Our under-18s coach reflects on our first win of the season against Southampton
bodyEn: Under-18s coach Josh Smith was pleased with his side’s spirited performance against Southampton, securing their first three points of the season.
Maalik Hashi scored the only goal of the game inside 15 minutes with a neat finish off the post and our young Gunners held on despite late Saints pressure.

"I thought it was a very positive start to the game. We've been speaking to the boys about how they start and today we had seven corners in the first 10 minutes, so in terms of how we started the game, it was very pleasing.

"In the first half, the build-up, finding the free player, using the third man and the entries into the final third were probably the best that we've seen. We're trying to encourage Mal [Maalik Hashi] to shoot from distance and have our midfielders arrive late into the box to score, so really pleased for Mal today.

"Second half, I thought it was a game where, if we take our chances, it could be two, three or four. I think the decision-making in the second half, sort of in and around the box, not taking those chances, gave Southampton a little bit of hope. But in terms of how the lads reacted and how we had to defend, we're pleased."
Our strong start was enough to earn our first U18 Premier League South win of the campaign, with our work in front of goal proving decisive.
Josh was pleased with the way we controlled the opening half, while admitting there was room for greater consistency after the interval.

"I thought there was a clear style in terms of how we built up and how we entered the final third, especially in the first half. Some of our decision-making, whether to play through or round over, and the technical execution of the players, was clean today.

“However, in the second half, I was a little bit disappointed because when we did win the ball back, we needed to judge whether it was a fast moment to go or whether we needed to slow it down. It was a contrast between the two halves, but for us as staff, we need to demand more consistency across both halves.”
Despite a tricky start to the season, Josh has also been encouraged by the group's progress during the opening weeks, with performances suggesting results would come.

The academy coach was delighted to see their efforts beat a Southampton side that entered the game with three wins from three. "I see a hungry group of players," he said. "Every single day they come into training and bring a mindset that they want to get better. That's all we can ask for from these young scholars.

"I see a real kind of perseverance in sticking to what we're doing. Recently, players and staff have been feeling a little down with the results, but we believe we can continue what we're doing and turn those performances into good results. I'm really, really pleased for the boys today."

items.titleEn: U18s report: Arsenal 1-0 Southampton
items.summaryEn: Our young Gunners beat the Saints to claim their first victory of the season
bodyEn: Our young Gunners found their first U18 Premier League South victory of the campaign with a 1-0 win at home to Southampton.
A so-far faultless Saints side came unstuck when Maalik Hashi put us in front early on, before a tight, goalless second half saw us hold on to claim all three points.
FIRST HALF
We made a positive start and took the lead on the quarter-hour mark when Hashi drove forward, cut inside onto his left foot and tucked a fine finish into the bottom corner via the post.

Our pressure continued through good link-up play between Luis Munoz and Hakeem Abubakar on the edge of the Saints’ box, with the latter playing a neat cutback to Jaden Maghoma, who was unable to keep his shot below the crossbar.

Hashi came close to doubling our advantage on the stroke of half-time, benefiting from a smart ball in the visitors' area before firing across the target, but his effort struck the wrong side of the woodwork and was cleared away.
SECOND HALF
Munoz looked determined to continue our strong first-half performance with a pair of long-range efforts, but neither troubled George Moloney in the Southampton net.
The Hampshire side began to grow into the affair from the hour mark onwards, as Walter Nutter forced Jack Porter into a diving save to keep us in front.

As we headed into the final minutes with our slender lead still intact, Munoz sent Hashi through with just the goalkeeper to beat, but the Saints stopper produced a good save to deny us some breathing space.

Porter was called into action late on when a short back pass allowed Ralph Brockway through on goal, but our no. 1 read the move well and was quick off his line to thwart the danger, ensuring our young Gunners claimed their first win of the season.
WHAT IT MEANS
Our first three points of the campaign see us climb into 10th place.
WHAT'S NEXT
We're back in U18 Premier League South action at home to Crystal Palace on Saturday, September 12.
Kick-off at the Sobha Realty Training Centre is scheduled for 11am (UK time).

Subs: Lupinski, Stachow, Arteta, Frohock.
Southampton XI: Moloney, Wells, Vallance, Martin (Afzal 45), Sewell, Nutter, Comley (Fletcher 60), Lovatt (Bariami 71), Kuzanga, Brockway, Parry.
Subs: Richardson, Lemon, Robinson.

items.titleEn: Preview: Brighton v Arsenal Women
items.summaryEn: Our 2026/27 Women’s Super League campaign begins against Brighton & Hove Albion at Broadfield Stadium, kicking off at 12pm on Sunday.
bodyEn: Our 2026/27 Women’s Super League campaign begins against Brighton & Hove Albion at Broadfield Stadium, kicking off at 12pm on Sunday.
We travel to Crawley off the back of a positive pre-season schedule, in which we beat Crystal Palace, Manchester City, Paris FC, Charlton Athletic and Everton.
The Seagulls were on similar form, beating Brann, Watford, Crystal Palace and Genk before losing 3-1 to Barcelona in the Joan Gamper Trophy.
SEAGULLS SWOOP

Brighton have been busy in the transfer market, landing signatures for goalkeeper Eleanor Heeps, defender Gabby George, midfielders Emilie Joramo, Lia Walti and Sophie Peskett, and forwards Nadia Krezyman and Emily Murphy.
Four players have left the club permanently, namely Sophie Baggaley, Libby Bance, Nadine Noordam and Rachel McLauchlan, while six others have gone out on loan.
Murphy, arriving from Newcastle United, isn’t taking long to make an impression, having scored in both of Brighton’s first two pre-season fixtures.
There’s been a surprise change in the dugout, with Arturo Ruiz coming in as manager to replace Dario Vidosic, who is seeking a new club.
WHAT THE MANAGERS SAY

Slegers: “The quality of players in the league, the quality of coaches, it’s all very exciting. But I mainly look at what we have, what we’re doing and what we’ve done in the last six weeks - and the desire, quality and alignment we’ve created within our squad.

“That’s what I’m really excited to see, that’s all good, all nice and that’s a great foundation, but now let’s go and play competitive games." - read every word of Renée’s pre-Brighton press conference.
Ruiz: “First of all, it's about having a strong psychological identity. We want a dressing room that is very unique and has a lot of great synergies between all of us.

“Talking about football, I want to be very unpredictable and having plans adapted to each of our rivals. We want to be very aggressive, to press high when necessary but also live comfortable in a medium block or some more conservative plans."
TEAM NEWS

Renée confirmed in her pre-match press conference that the players currently completing rehabilitation programmes are Daphne van Domselaar, Katie Reid and Michelle Agyemang, and that everyone else is fit to play.
FACTS AND STATS
We will kick-off a WSL campaign with an away game for the first time in 11 seasons (excl. Spring Series), last doing so with a 1-1 draw against Notts County in 2015.

We went unbeaten in each of our final 17 league games last season (W13 D4) and could equal our second longest run without defeat in the competition, set in December 2021 and November 2022; our longest unbeaten run in the competition is 19 matches between August 2011 and October 2012.

In the 2025/26 Women’s Super League campaign, we recorded the most high turnovers (314), goal ending high turnovers (9) and recorded the highest field tilt percentage for the third successive season (77%).

Georgia Stanway played the most passes (1992), the most passes into the final third (449) and made the most carries (442) of any player across Europe’s big five leagues last season, while recording the joint-second most assists (9) in the 2025/26 Bundesliga.

Since Renée Slegers took charge of her first WSL game with us in October 2024, only Chelsea (100) have won more points in the English top-flight than ourselves (94), who also boast the most goals (111) and best goal difference (+75) in that period.
MATCH OFFICIALS
Kirsty Dowle has been appointed to take charge of our first match of the season. She’s already been busy in the men’s League One and EFL Trophy across August.
She last saw over one of our fixtures when we won 2-0 away to London City Lionesses in March.

bodyEn: For many people connected to Arsenal, it has been a time to remember the old line from Arsène Wenger. “We live in a society of ‘news’,” the club’s former manager once said, and by that he meant new things – the shinier the better.

Nowhere is the obsession more obvious than in the transfer market, when a club simply has to add new faces. These days, it feels as though some fans prefer them to be signed as late as possible in the summer window to ensure a positive narrative after the deadline; to maximise the potential to generate momentum. Recency bias is powerful.

Wenger’s tone was disapproving. The next big thing is not always thus. What you already have should not be undervalued or taken for granted. It struck a chord with Mikel Arteta, which everybody in the room for his press conference to preview Sunday’s home game against Chelsea could feel because it moved him out of succinct answer territory.

The Arsenal manager enters the match having won three out of three this season – including the Community Shield victory over Manchester City – without conceding a goal. His club, of course, ended their long wait for the Premier League title last May when they chased away all manner of demons. They are hot favourites to win it again.

At Aston Villa on Monday night, Arteta introduced two of Spain’s World Cup winning squad – Mikel Merino and Martín Zubimendi – from the bench. Plus the marquee summer signing, Bruno Guimarães. Plus Eberechi Eze. Plus another high-profile new boy, Ezri Konsa. Arsenal’s strength in depth is really something.

Their squad is surely stronger now than it was at the end of last season. Does Arteta feel that? “Yes I do,” he said. “We are better equipped. We have more players available. We have increased the quality and we have increased the leadership in the team as well, which is very important.”

So, why the angst among supporters after the transfer window closed, which was probably nearer to hysteria in some cases? “It’s human nature,” Arteta said. “When you talk to people and you ask them … normally, it’s: ‘OK, what is on your bucket list?’ People write a lot about the bucket list. And sometimes we forget the reverse bucket list, which is the things that you already have in your life that are incredible. But you put so much emphasis on them [the bucket list items] that nothing seems to be enough.

“It’s very important to value what we have, what we have created together. To have ambition is great, especially to evolve the things we already have within the club. But listen – don’t lose perspective to what we already have, which is amazing.”

Arsenal are indisputably better in defence with Konsa and in midfield with Guimarães. The worry is the front line where it has been one in (Christos Tzolis) and four out (Leandro Trossard, Gabriel Martinelli, Gabriel Jesus and Ethan Nwaneri).

The reasoning for each departure was difficult to fault. Trossard is 31, he had one year on his contract and Besiktas offered £15.3m. Tzolis felt like a fine replacement for him. Martinelli scored once in the league last season, although he contributed four in the FA Cup and six in the Champions League. Arsenal got £60m from Al-Hilal for him; a club record sale.

As an aside, Arteta mentioned how Arsenal had “made a move last summer” – a reference to their lavish spending – and there has been an acknowledgement within the club that there had to be a balancing this time.

Jesus started nine games in all competitions last season, scoring six goals. He, too, was into the final year of his deal, and he was one of the club’s highest earners. At one stage, it looked as though he might look to see out his contract and in the end, a £8.6m deal with Barcelona rising to £12.9m suited all parties. Nwaneri barely played for Arsenal last season, going to Marseille on loan in January. Another loan, this time to Borussia Dortmund, made sense, particularly as there is a January recall clause.

Yet the weight of the outgoing numbers makes it hard to say Arsenal are stronger in this department and Arteta was in no mood to over-promise here. “It’s another question and we have to prove in that particular position whether we are better or not,” he said. “Let’s see. I understand the point of view [about the number of departures] but we have to understand as well the amount of minutes that those players played. And the ones that were injured last season, especially in the first six months. It is what it is.”There is the belief at Arsenal that Eze can in essence replace Martinelli on the left, albeit he is a different kind of player. Arsenal can perhaps play in a different way, with Riccardo Calafiori stepping up more from left-back. There is the hope that with a reshaped medical staff, the team can have a better run on the injury front – specifically with Bukayo Saka, Martin Ødegaard and Kai Havertz having uninterrupted seasons. The fear is that more problems will undermine them.

What has coloured the post-transfer window vibe is the failure to add a big-name attacker, to make a real statement signing. If Arteta did have a bucket list, then a game-changer for the front line would have been on it. Arsenal did try; they reached for stars such as Vinícius Júnior, Julián Alvarez and Morgan Rogers. Arteta even suggested that this kind of intent was progress. It is a tough sell when the glamour targets remain elusive.

There was a point in July when Arsenal thought there was more of a chance they would get Vinícius than not. Then Real Madrid made him a new contract offer and he signed it. Alvarez just did not want to come, and the case of Rogers boiled down to the numbers. Arsenal offered £80m to Aston Villa for him and no more. Chelsea ended up going to £117m. They overpaid. But then they announced a deal with Villa two days later to loan Alejandro Garnacho there with a conditional purchase obligation, valuing the winger at £40m. Chelsea found a way to get Rogers. Arsenal did not. He will be a major subplot on Sunday .

There were moments when Arteta dropped his usual ultra-positive outlook and offered little peeks behind the curtain, including when he suggested that reporters speak to the sporting director, Andrea Berta, or the co-chair Josh Kroenke about why it was so difficult to close deals for the very elite.

“To get these deals done in this market is complicated,” he said. “I don’t know how it looks from the outside but we have put in everything that we possibly could to make those deals happen and we made most of them happen. We have been very efficient with what Andrea has done in the market again. It has been incredible, the support of all the club and that’s it. It’s not perfect but it doesn’t need to be perfect.”
Arteta believes that Arsenal have enough.

items.titleEn: Preview: Arsenal v Chelsea
items.summaryEn: Get all the lowdown on our Sunday opponents as we take on Chelsea
bodyEn: After picking up our second Premier League win of the season at Aston Villa, we return to Emirates Stadium to take on Chelsea in a huge London derby.
Both sides have made a perfect start to the league season, with our opponents beating Fulham and Brighton in their first two matches.
Chelsea were one of the busiest clubs in the transfer window, but after that closed this week, it's all about the football as the two sides go head-to-head on Sunday at 4.30pm.
ALONSO SETTLES QUICKLY
Chelsea missed out on European football last season as new manager Xabi Alonso became the sixth permanent boss in six years.

The Spaniard, who grew up in the same region as our boss, Mikel Arteta, brought in 11 players, including former Gunners Emiliano Martinez and Danny Welbeck, as well as Premier League players Morgan Rogers, Jordan Henderson and Maxence Lacroix.
It's been so far, so good, for the former Real Madrid and Bayer Leverkusen boss, who picked up two victories in his opening two games as manager.

It started with west London derby success against Fulham, with front three Morgan Rogers, Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro all finding the net. They followed that up with a thrilling 4-3 triumph over Brighton.
It means that Chelsea join us with six points out of six going into their trip north, where they last beat us 2-0 in August 2021.
WHAT THE MANAGERS SAY

Arteta: "I love my players, that's what I can say. I think at the end of the season we'll put everybody in their place and let's trust them. Let's make sure that we are right behind them and we do everything we can to help the incredible talent that they have.

"The the two games that they [Chelsea] played, they scored very, very early and that changes the momentum and the shift of the game. But they are capable and he [Alonso] is capable of playing in various ways. That's been a really successful match so far."
Alonso: "We can be very happy with the whole transfer window. What we started talking about in May/early June - many things we have.
"It is a very balanced phase one we have made in this transfer window. Phase one is completed; it's a good one for now and for the future."
TEAM NEWS

During his pre-match press conference, Mikel Arteta said that Bruno Guimaraes picked up a knock in our 1-0 win at Aston Villa, with a decision on his inclusion to come this weekend. He also said the same of Cristhian Mosquera, who was forced off at Villa Park. Elsewhere, Jurrien Timber was in training as he continues his recovery. William Saliba is a longer-term absentee, with Mikel positive about his development.
He said: "The progression has been really positive in the last few weeks, but we need to wait and see how that one reacts when we start to put some load into it."

As for Chelsea, they are waiting on a late fitness test of midfielder Moises Caicedo, who went off in their 4-3 victory over Brighton & Hove Albion. The Blues will also be without Jordan Henderson, who picked up an injury during the World Cup with England, but Alonso admitted he's getting closer and closer to first-team action.
TALKING TACTICS

Adrian Clarke: "Chelsea’s new-look front three are dripping with match-winning talent. England duo Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer love to float around between the lines in support of striker Joao Pedro, and as a trio they are flying right now.
"Across just 180 minutes of Premier League football alongside one another they have delivered five goals and four assists combined.

"Chelsea’s attacking wingbacks have also been bright, with Pedro Neto and Jorrel Hato catching the eye. Portugal international Neto was super-dangerous inside the final third last time out but is not a natural defender. So, will Alonso trust him in that role here at Emirates Stadium this afternoon. If Neto starts, it will certainly signify the Spaniard’s intent to attack us at every opportunity.

"Central midfield looks like an area of possible weakness. Enzo Fernandez has left the club, while Moises Caicedo has also suffered with injury issues early in the campaign. This means the likes of Romeo Lavia, Malo Gusto, Reece James and Valentin Barco have had to fill the void. They are all good players in their own right, but as it stands Chelsea do not have a strong midfield pairing with vast experience of either playing together, or even occupying that position.

"Right across the team there has been a lot of change, and that is almost certain to create teething issues. Conceding twice from set pieces already and looking quite nervy from balls sent into the box, there is a sense that Alonso’s men have some work to do on their defensive game. "
FACTS AND STATS
MATCH OFFICIALS

Chris Kavanagh is the man with the whistle for the London derby. He has taken charge of this fixture on two previous occasions, the most recent coming in March 2025, when Mikel Merino scored the winner in a 1-0 victory for us.
Kavanagh has refereed one game so far this season, a 1-1 draw between Bournemouth and Everton. The last time he officiated an Arsenal match was in May 2026, when we beat West Ham United 1-0.
Referee: Chris KavanaghAssistants: Dan Cook, Tim WoodFourth official: Tom BramallVAR: Darren EnglandAssistant VAR: Constantine Hatzidakis
CHELSEA RECORD
Since losing to Chelsea in August 2021, we've undergone an incredible 11-game unbeaten run against the Blues that's spanned five years and nine different managers, interim or permanent, at the helm.
Those 11 unbeaten games have come across the Premier League and Carabao Cup, where we ousted the Blues 4-2 on aggregate in last season's semi-final.
Our last victory against Chelsea took place in March 2026, where William Saliba and Jurrien Timber headed us to victory at Emirates Stadium.
LIVE COVERAGE

A return to Emirates Stadium can only mean one thing, our preview show is back, Live from N5. Packed with special guests, analysis and much more, head to Arsenal.com and The Arsenal app (download now on iOS/Android) for our preview show. Then, just before kick off, tune into Dan Roebuck and Adrian Clarke to take you through the on-field action against the Blues.
You can also find out which broadcasters are showing the action live, wherever you are in the world.

bodyEn: Chelsea thought they had little chance of signing Morgan Rogers at the start of the summer. Xabi Alonso and the club’s recruitment team had the England international as a priority target but a deal seemed unlikely. Chelsea had endured a disappointing season, missing out on European football after finishing 10th, and their expectation was that Rogers would leave Aston Villa for Arsenal.

It was towards the end of the World Cup that Chelsea were made aware of a window of opportunity. Although Arsenal could claim to be London’s top dogs after winning the Premier League they dithered in talks with Villa, raising the prospect of another club stepping in.

Mikel Arteta talked about being bold in the market after Arsenal’s defeat by Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League final. Arteta wanted more in attack. A new option on the left was a priority; Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli were up for sale and everything pointed towards Arsenal making their move for Rogers at the end of June.

Yet the lines became blurred. Arsenal had a fee of £80m in mind, while Villa wanted more, particularly after Nottingham Forest sold Elliot Anderson to Manchester City for £116m. Time dragged on. How serious were Arsenal? There was also interest in Julián Alvarez, Vinícius Júnior and Bradley Barcola. Villa waited and the price for Rogers went up. Arsenal, beaten to the punch in the end, will have a look at what they could have won when Chelsea and Rogers visit the Emirates Stadium on Sunday.

Chelsea were decisive. They were tracking Rogers before he left Middlesbrough for Villa in February 2024. Joe Shields, one of Chelsea’s five sporting directors, worked with Rogers at Manchester City’s academy. The signing was not done on a whim. Chelsea have a good relationship with Villa’s owners and moved quickly after opening club-to-club talks a day after Rogers played in England’s World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina. The fee was £117m and Chelsea did not struggle to convince Rogers. Alonso wooed him and the deal was confirmed five days after negotiations began.

There was no last-ditch move from Arsenal. They signed Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge for £34m two days later and focused on other targets. When the window closed, though, Arteta’s options on the left looked a little light. Martinelli and Trossard left but only Tzolis arrived. Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke are alternatives. It is hard not to feel that Arsenal could have done with Rogers, even though Chelsea have paid a high price for him.

It remains to be seen whether the 24-year-old can prove he merits becoming the third-most expensive player in English football history. For context, the fee is the consequence of the market threatening to rise out of control and the money spent on many players starting to feel meaningless. It is worth pointing out, too, that money flowed back and forth between Chelsea and Villa all summer. Even so the price will follow Rogers around, so it is just as well he has made an excellent start.

Rogers has been involved in four of Chelsea’s seven goals in their first two league games. He scored in the 3-2 win at Fulham and later combined with João Pedro to set up Cole Palmer’s goal. He created Pedro Neto’s goal in last weekend’s 4-3 win over Brighton and played a key role when Jorrel Hato played in João Pedro to score.

Chelsea have thrilled in attack so far, João Pedro, Rogers and Palmer combining to devastating effect. Alonso, an adaptable manager, wants more control but his transitional football has been a delight. Chelsea were mannered and controlled during Enzo Maresca’s time in charge. It is felt that Alonso has recognised the Premier League’s shift towards power and athleticism. Rogers fits into the Spaniard’s system. Thomas Tuchel loves Rogers for his connectivity and pressing. It is significant that England’s energy levels rose in their quarter-final against Norway after the introduction of Rogers and Djed Spence late in the second half.

Chelsea needed more strength, more speed. Rogers, able to play anywhere in attacking midfield or as a No 8, looks a better fit in Alonso’s 3-4-2-1 than Enzo Fernández, sold this week to Manchester City for £125m. He has played with Palmer as one of the No 10s but has a responsibility to drift left, a role that is unlikely to have suited Fernández. Arsenal’s impeccable defence will be tested by Chelsea’s front three.

The Rogers-Palmer partnership has clicked. They are old friends and banter over the “ice cold” celebration. Rogers is a bubbly character and can get on with anyone. Chelsea are keen to improve the culture in the dressing room. It is felt that Alonso has shifted the mood after last year’s rebellions. The squad are united. It is one of the reasons why Chelsea decided to sell Fernández on deadline day. They did not need the headache of reintegrating the Argentinian.

This is a fresh start. The signing of Rogers, who was the Professional Footballers’ Association’s young player of the year in 2025, was a sign of Chelsea’s intent. Rogers was one of the best players in the Premier League last season. He grew under Unai Emery and scored when Villa beat Freiburg in the Europa League final in May.

It was one of Rogers’ less eye-catching goals: a clever jab at the near post from a low cross. There was a period last season when he could not stop scoring from long range but Rogers has spoken about wanting scruffier goals and he arrived at the far post to open his Chelsea account against Fulham.

Rogers is embracing the challenge. At Arsenal he would have been slotting into the finished article. Arsenal have reached the summit. Chelsea are beginning their climb under Alonso. Rogers, who has played in the Championship and had a loan in League One, rather liked the idea of starting lower down.

items.titleEn: 'Pass from the gods' - Reliving our 03/04 Chelsea clashes
items.summaryEn: We take a look back at our pivotal clashes with Chelsea from the 03/04 season
bodyEn: Arsenal and Chelsea faced one another in no fewer than five high-octane clashes during the 2003/04 season. Perhaps understandably, the summer noise in 2003 had centred upon billionaire Roman Abramovich’s £140m purchase of Chelsea.

It proved to be a takeover which changed the face of football across the globe, and instantly gave manager Claudio Ranieri an enormous transfer kitty to spend. Following an estimated £153million splurge, in came an array of football talent from home and abroad, including winger Damien Duff, defenders Wayne Bridge and Glen Johnson, midfielders Claude Makélélé and Juan Sebastián Verón, and forwards Hernán Crespo and Adrian Mutu.

By contrast, the Gunners spent just £1.5 million that summer - on goalkeeper Jens Lehmann - who replaced Manchester City-bound David Seaman, and in January purchased Spanish winger Jose Antonio Reyes for an initial £10 million.
"Of course we were very much aware of what Chelsea were doing," explained skipper Patrick Vieira, "but we were keen to show that we still had what it took to win the big prizes."

When the two sides met at Highbury on October 18, 2003, both were unbeaten in the league. On a bright and breezy day, Edu’s deflected free kick gave Arsenal the lead, before Argentinian star Crespo, signed from Serie A giants Inter Milan, equalised for Chelsea with a magnificent swirling drive from just outside the box.

The game appeared to be petering out, before Chelsea goalkeeper Claudio Cudicini’s error on 75 minutes gifted the game to Arsene Wenger’s men. Following Dennis Bergkamp’s quick free kick, Robert Pires’ misplaced cross was fumbled by the Blues’ number one, and Thierry Henry tapped the ball home.

The 2-1 win meant that Chelsea were still seeking their first Premiership victory at Highbury after 12 visits and the Gunners had delivered the first serious dent to the growing title optimism at Stamford Bridge.

Less than a week after new signing Jose Antonio Reyes’s rapid double meant that Arsenal had ended Chelsea’s FA Cup ambitions for a fourth successive season in a 2-1 win at Highbury, the two sides met once again at Stamford Bridge in a crunch Premier League clash on February 21, 2004.
Chelsea still harboured league title ambitions, and an Eidur Gudjohnsen goal after just 27 seconds stunned the visitors. But Arsenal fought back in spectacular style.
A sumptuous pass with the outside of his foot from Dennis Bergkamp put in Patrick Vieira, who calmly slotted home past Neil Sullivan to grab his first goal of the season.
"The pass from Dennis was from the gods," Vieira smiled. "It was one of our best goals that season I think."
After Sullivan fumbled Gilberto’s in-swinging corner, Edu lashed the ball home from four yards to give Arsenal a 2-1 win, meaning that we’d stretched our lead at the top to seven points.

The Gunners romped to the Premier League title unbeaten, finishing eleven points ahead of runners-up Chelsea, although Ranieri’s side knocked Arsenal out of the Champions League at the quarter-final stage, before themselves losing to Monaco in the semi-final.
Their league positions would be reversed the following season, with Chelsea ending the 2004/05 campaign 12 points ahead of Wenger’s men and winning a first league title since 1955.

Now managed by Jose Mourinho, the Blues had embarked upon another enormous spending spree. But in the 2003/04 campaign, the legendary Invincibles’ two league victories over Chelsea demonstrated that, in Gilberto’s words: "We were still kings of both London and England."

bodyEn: Our young Gunners look to bounce back against Southampton when they continue their U18 Premier League South campaign on Saturday, September 5.
The match will take place at the Sobha Realty Training Centre, with kick-off scheduled for 1pm (UK time).
Yet to claim a win from their opening three games, our under-18s’ only point so far came in a goalless draw with West Bromwich Albion on the opening day.
Last weekend, despite taking the lead away at Brighton and Hove Albion through Abraham Owusu-Gyasi’s second-half finish, the Seagulls fought back to win 2-1.
THE OPPOSITION
After finishing seventh last term, the Saints have made a perfect start to the new season, winning all three games and averaging five goals scored per match.
In August, the south coast side hit four past both Brentford and Crystal Palace, before an eleven-goal thriller against Norwich City ended in a 7-4 victory a week ago.

The high-scoring outfit have also been placed in Group D of the U18 Premier League Cup, alongside Brentford, Manchester City and Burnley, with their opening tie against the Clarets set for next month.
We last faced the Hampshire side in January, narrowly losing 1-0 at the Staplewood Training Ground after Thierry Rohart-Brown found the net early in the second half.

The action gets underway from 1pm (UK), with live updates available on our Academy X account and a full match report shortly after the final whistle.
Post-match, don't miss exclusive interviews with one of our academy coaches and young Gunners, as well as highlights of all the key action on The Arsenal app and Arsenal.com.

There were signs of promise against Nottingham Forest, where he set up the second equaliser and would have had a goal of his own if not for an offside in the buildup. Bruno Fernandes showed there is plenty of fun for an attacking midfielder to have against Ipswich and Wirtz can follow suit as a protagonist. Liverpool have drawn both their opening fixtures 2-2 and need something to kickstart their campaign, with a Friday night visit to promoted opposition a fine place to do so. Wirtz should cause problems but, if he does not, the internal competition will be after his spot. Will Unwin
Ipswich v Liverpool (Friday 8pm, all times BST)

Verticality, intensity and hard pressing are likely to be the order of the day at St James’ Park, where two German graduates of the Red Bull stable meet on Saturday at lunchtime. Newcastle’s new manager, Matthias Jaissle, is a former head coach of Red Bull Salzburg, while Bournemouth’s Marco Rose has managed Salzburg and RB Leipzig. “We have the same idea of how we want to play football,” said Jaissle – and Rose knows what to expect from Eddie Howe’s successor. “Matthias and me were several years in the style of Red Bull,” he said. “Everyone knows how we work. You can see it clearly. He’s a good coach. He’s brought his ideas really quickly into the Newcastle team. They are playing quite intense, they have clear pressing patterns that are different from before.” Louise Taylor
Newcastle v Bournemouth (Saturday 12.30pm)

Saturday’s meeting between two of the Premier League’s best-run clubs, Brentford and Sunderland, promises to one of the best contests of the weekend, with both sides physical, technical and superbly coached. Brentford, in particular, have made a terrific start to the season, the left side of their team looking especially dangerous. Keane Lewis-Potter provides impetus from full-back, with Mamadou Sangaré backing up strong ball-winning and carrying with intelligent passing, while Kevin Schade offers a threat in behind and, increasingly, in front of goal. All of which suggests a difficult afternoon for Thomas Meunier, Sunderland’s likely right-back who, at 34, has plenty of experience but might struggle with the athletic questions asked of him. He will, though, be able to rely on assistance from Noah Sadiki, whose nous, work ethic and running power will be invaluable in defending Sunderland’s right flank. How that battle plays out will go a long way towards deciding the game. Daniel Harris
Brentford v Sunderland (Saturday 3pm)

We can be sure any player Brighton buy has delivered the data metrics employed by the owner, Tony Bloom. But Chema Andrés, the 21-year-old midfielder just signed from Stuttgart, also nails the eye test. He was signed for £18.9m and it’s already tempting to speculate how sizeable the mark-up will be when Brighton sell him on. If we remember we’re talking about a sport, it’s impossible not to be excited about what the former Real Madrid academy midfielder brings to Fabian Hürzeler’s team. A No 6 of the old school, Chema offers economical movement but extravagant intelligence, evident in his passing and anticipation. Even if this weekend’s game against Leeds comes too early for him to be handed a start, he will make an impact soon enough. DH
Brighton v Leeds (Saturday 3pm)

It’s been a tricky summer for Crystal Palace despite their Conference League win. Oliver Glasner has gone, with two key defenders in Daniel Muñoz and Maxence Lacroix also departing and Jean-Philippe Mateta and Ismaïla Sarr trying their best to do likewise. This upheaval has left Pierre Sage, whose existing relationship with Malick Fofana wasn’t enough to secure the Lyon winger’s signature, with major problems. The former Lens coach is seeking to replace the club’s most successful manager while learning what works in a new league, with new players and without three mainstays. It wasn’t especially surprising to see Palace lose their first two matches, while Fulham have also been beaten twice while seeking to bed in a new coach and arrivals. More troubling for both teams is that the promoted sides look competitive. Hull and Ipswich have performed well and won games, while Coventry are better than they’ve shown so far. Though it’s far too early to talk about relegation, this already feels like a game of significance for two sides struggling for momentum. DH
Fulham v Crystal Palace (Saturday 3pm)

Manchester City spent more than £300m on new midfielders in this transfer window, but look light in the No 6 role, with Rodri and Nico González both departing. Ayyoub Bouaddi, bought as Rodri’s long-term successor, is only 18, so Enzo Maresca’s plan is to ease him into first-team action. The Manchester City manager deployed Marc Guéhi in a holding midfield role against Bournemouth, and is also confident Nico O’Reilly can switch from left-back to operate there. O’Reilly may line up at the base of midfield for Coventry’s visit, with City seeking a third straight win. Maresca is also not fazed by Omar Marmoush’s departure on an initial loan to Spurs, with Iliman Ndiaye arriving on deadline day and Antoine Semenyo also an able deputy centre-forward if Erling Haaland is unavailable. Jamie Jackson
Manchester City v Coventry (Saturday 3pm)

Liam Delap came off the bench against Liverpool and helped create Nottingham Forest’s second goal with quick thinking from a throw-in. The striker cost £45m from Chelsea but missed out on an intense pre-season after Xabi Alonso decided he was surplus to requirements, so needs to build fitness. Considering Tottenham’s major flaws thus far, it would make sense for Delap to be given the chance to spearhead the Forest attack. The former England Under-21s striker is the ideal No 9, quick, strong and a capable finisher, but needs to get all these attributes sharpened up. An outing against fragile opposition could speed up the process. Tottenham are bottom of the league having conceded five and scored none in two games, and compared with Chris Wood or Igor Jesus, Delap is a far scarier foe, as Oliver Glasner will know. WU
Nottingham Forest v Tottenham (Saturday 3pm)

They may have nabbed two wins in as many games upon their return to the Premier League but Hull were still not happy with their squad, seven new players arriving in the final week of the window. That means the Tigers have made 19 signings since promotion, which is an impressive turnover in personnel. Sergej Jakirovic needs to decide whether to incorporate these potential upgrades into his starting XI as soon as possible or make them earn the shirts from those who have accumulated six points. No one has let down the head coach or the fans over 180 minutes, so it would be harsh to drop anyone but, equally, having spent so much money on acquisitions, it could be argued that the sooner they get on the pitch, the quicker they will gel. It is not an easy decision for Jakirovic to make but he values loyalty and will want to challenge the mentality of the new arrivals – no one will walk into the side he has built. WU
Hull v Aston Villa (Saturday 5.30pm)

There are parallels between Manchester United’s visit to Hill Dickinson Stadium and their 3-0 win at Goodison Park in 2023 in the sense they will face a furious Everton crowd, and for the second time in four seasons the anger will not be directed towards them. Three years ago it was the Premier League in Evertonians’ sights after the record 10-point deduction that had just been imposed on the club. This time it is Everton’s owners, The Friedkin Group, in the firing line after the club’s shambolic end to the transfer window. There will be no flag displays inside the stadium after the group responsible for organising them, the 1878s, withdrew their support and there are calls for a “not a pound in the ground” campaign in response to the owners making a profit on transfers while leaving David Moyes with a weaker squad. Everton have started the season positively on the pitch, but are now surrounded by problems of their owners’ making. Andy Hunter
Everton v Manchester United (Sunday 2pm)

You have to go back to the start of the 2021-22 season, when Arsenal had Rob Holding and Pablo Marí in central defence, for the last time Chelsea beat their north London rivals, a run of 11 matches in all competitions. But they came close to ending that sequence in the 1-1 draw at Stamford Bridge last season before things began to unravel for Enzo Maresca, and the Italian’s successor, Xabi Alonso, will head to the Emirates to face his old friend Mikel Arteta in a competitive match for the first time as a manager full of confidence after winning his opening two games. Chelsea’s new-look front three of Cole Palmer, João Pedro and Morgan Rogers can certainly cause Arsenal problems, although the question is whether a defence that has conceded five goals can keep out the champions. Ed Aarons
Arsenal v Chelsea (Sunday 4.30pm)

bodyEn: Arsenal have confirmed Gabriel Martinelli has joined the Saudi Arabian side Al-Hilal for £60m. It is understood the deal for Brazil forward includes a sell-on clause.

Martinelli, who joined Arsenal from Ituano in 2019, has fallen down the pecking order at the Emirates despite being part of the squad that won the Premier League title last season. His fee surpasses the previous record £40m received by Arsenal when they sold Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain to Liverpool in 2017.

Martinelli is believed to have signed a four-year contract worth about £17m a season. His move was widely expected after Arsenal agreed a deal last week and has gone through before the transfer window in Saudi Arabia closes on Sunday.

The 25-year-old joins his Brazil teammate Gabriel Jesus in leaving Arsenal this week, the striker having moved to Barcelona for £8.6m. The Premier League champions also sold Fábio Vieira to Hamburg on deadline day but decided against bringing in players.

Arsenal are believed to have received about £3m from Brook Norton-Cuffy’s £14m move from Genoa to Hull owing to a sell-on clause in the England Under-21 defender’s contract but missed out on about £7m when Folarin Balogun move to Everton collapsed.

Tottenham have omitted Richarlison from their Premier League squad, with the striker not a part of their plans for the season. They could have accommodated him for the first-half of the campaign because one of their 17 senior non-homegrown players – Xavi Simons – is out until March or April, according to the manager, Roberto Di Zerbi, with an anterior cruciate ligament injury.

Spurs made clear to Richarlison before the closure of the transfer window in England on Tuesday night that he would not be included so he could arrange a move. He was unable to do so, with one to his former club, Everton, not happening. He is the subject of firm interest from Trabzonspor in Turkey, where the window remains open until Friday night.

Richarlison posted a message on social media on Monday in which he said he would not allow anybody to decide his future for him. He talked about his commitment to Spurs; how “when everything here was falling apart and they needed me, I stayed and gave my life”.

bodyEn: When Mikel Arteta revealed before Arsenal’s win at Aston Villa that he had pleaded with the Premier League to introduce bigger matchday squads, the final 24 hours of the transfer window was not quite what he would have had in mind. A deadline day on which Manchester City matched the British record to sign Enzo Fernández from Chelsea for £125m came and went as Arsenal allowed Gabriel Jesus and Ethan Nwaneri to leave without bringing in replacements.

With Gabriel Martinelli joining Al-Hilal for £60m on Thursday, there are question marks about the depth of the champions’ squad, despite Arteta still having at least two options for each position. Eberechi Eze will provide competition on the left for the new boy Christos Tzolis, and the manager has a plethora of central midfielders at his disposal after the arrival of Bruno Guimarães from Newcastle, but there is not much room for manoeuvre should Arsenal experience injuries in attack like they have for the past two seasons.

Arteta had been clear after the Villa game when asked whether he hoped to bring in more players. “We know that the depth has to be really big when you are fighting for four competitions in the manner that we play as well, so we’re going to try to do that,” he said.

Yet none arrived as Arsenal passed up the opportunity to bring in Malick Fofana owing to what it is understood were Arteta’s doubts over whether the Belgium forward would improve the squad, with Sunderland eventually beating Crystal Palace to his signature in dramatic scenes. The fallout has prompted some Arsenal supporters to question the wisdom of spending most of the summer, after missing out on Morgan Rogers to Chelsea, chasing “dream” transfer targets such as Vinícius Júnior and Julián Alvarez, with the sporting director, Andrea Berta, most in the firing line.

The Italian’s arrival from Atlético Madrid in March 2025 was heralded as a coup by many. Berta’s decisiveness last summer enabled Arsenal to rack up a net spend of more than £250m – comfortably outstripping their rivals – on players such as Eze, Viktor Gyökeres and Martín Zubimendi.

This summer the Premier League champions were quick off the mark to replace Leandro Trossard with Tzolis, then added Guimarães, before buying Ezri Konsa to cover the long-term absence of William Saliba, but the lack of attacking reinforcements on deadline day was eye-catching.

Offloading Jesus, one of the club’s highest earners, saved wages, and Martinelli’s departure as the club’s record sale would reduce Arsenal’s net spend to £78m – less than Brentford’s – compared with £162m at City, who spent more than £300m recalibrating their midfield. Iliman Ndiaye, who joined City from Everton for £65m, was another player on Arsenal’s shortlist who they opted against.

There can be no questioning Kroenke Sports Entertainment’s commitment to the cause, Arsenal having the second-highest net spend over past five seasons at more than £680m. Yet it will not have escaped the attention of some fans that it was confirmed on deadline day that KSE will expand its sporting empire with the purchase of the Major League Baseball side the Los Angeles Angels, for a reported $4bn (£3bn). With an estimated value of $26bn, it is not as if it cannot afford that.

Even before Arsenal wrapped up their first title for 22 years in May, the co-chair Josh Kroenke promised that “there will be no standing still when the season ends”, and bringing in Premier League-ready players such as Konsa and Guimarães was a statement of intent. However, the inability to attract real star quality in attack is an issue considering the heavy burden on Bukayo Saka after a couple of injury-hit campaigns. Kenan Yildiz could have fitted the bill but Juventus were not interested in selling the Turkey forward, and Alvarez made plain he wanted only Barcelona.

Arsenal struggled to break teams down during the second half of last season and became heavily reliant on their set-piece prowess, although a rejuvenated Martin Ødegaard has started the campaign promisingly.

Martinelli has failed in recent seasons to replicate his form of the 2022-23 season, when he scored 15 Premier League goals, but his pace off the bench often caused problems for teams who were chasing the game. None of Arteta’s remaining options possess that commodity, though Tzolis showed before a difficult half at Villa that he has the ability to create and score goals.

Eze, who missed in the shootout that decided the Champions League final against Paris Saint-Germain after coming off the bench, replaced the Greece forward against Villa and played a key role in Saka’s winner. Even after his heroics against Tottenham last season, scoring five goals against the team who were gazumped for his signature, the England forward has not nailed down a starting spot in the most important games. Eze could end up being the biggest beneficiary of Arsenal’s transfer inactivity along with Max Dowman, the 16-year-old who has yet to make an appearance this season.
After a summer of transition among their rivals, Arteta is banking on continuity to stay ahead of the pack.

They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. It is all change at Villa and, although a little trepidation is inevitable, a refresh was probably overdue. At the same time, Unai Emery did not want to lose so many key players and Villa’s manager has made clear there is no such thing as a transition season in his eyes. Villa have generated about £300m from the sales of nine players and brought in 10 at a cost of about £250m. Villa have lowered their wage bill and changed the profile of their squad. Zion Suzuki, Ibrahim Mbaye and Johan Manzambi, names on the lips of Villa’s rivals, are particularly exciting signings. Last summer there was concern Villa had gone stale and 12 months ago they ended up fretting on deadline day – Harvey Elliott and Jadon Sancho joined on loan – but there was no such chaos this time. Perhaps Bournemouth’s best business was keeping hold of their coveted key players, chiefly Eli Junior Kroupi, Rayan, Alex Scott and Tyler Adams. Bournemouth rejected bids from Chelsea for Scott and stayed true to their plan of resisting offers to give Marco Rose the best chance of succeeding, with the club attempting to juggle European competition and the league for the first time. The arrival of the Portugal centre-back António Silva, 22, from Benfica looks a typically smart replacement for Marcos Senesi, 29. bodyEn: Aston Villa completed the signings of Ibrahim Mbaye and Taylor Harwood-Bellis on deadline day, with Unai Emery confident that the club’s radical summer overhaul has left Villa in position to replicate their recent success. Villa, who have lost both of their Premier League games this campaign, have qualified for the Champions League in two of the past three seasons and won their first major trophy in 30 years after lifting the Europa League.

The £47m arrival of the 18-year-old winger Mbaye from Paris Saint-Germain and £25m deal for Harwood-Bellis from Southampton represented Villa’s ninth and 10th summer signings respectively. Villa had generated more than £300m from the sales of nine players, six of whom started the Europa League triumph in Istanbul in May: Morgan Rogers, Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans, Lucas Digne and Emiliano Martínez all departed Villa Park in recent weeks, Rogers and Martinez joining Chelsea.

Watkins’s £50m exit to the Saudi Pro League club Al-Hilal, after rejecting Villa’s offer of a new contract, led to Villa signing Nicolas Jackson for an initial £47.5m that could rise to a club-record £65m. Earlier in the window, Villa signed Johan Manzambi for a club-record £52m from Freiburg but the Switzerland midfielder is yet to make his debut as he continues his recovery from a knee injury he sustained at the World Cup.

After the 1-0 home defeat by Arsenal on Monday, Emery struck an upbeat tone. “We are happy how we are closing the transfer window,” the Villa manager said. “We are not regretting anything and the players who are joining are players that should be enough to rebuild the team with the structure we want. I think we replaced the players as we planned.”

Zion Suzuki, a £30m arrival from Parma, made his Villa debut against Arsenal and Villa’s new No 1 accepts the task of replacing Martínez is a “good challenge”. “It was my priority to play games so that is why I made the decision and I played in Belgium for one year, in Parma for two years,” said the 24-year-old, who joined Villa after a move to PSG collapsed in the final stages.

“In the end I am here and playing for Villa. I just wanted to come here for this club. There are so many expectations. It is not easy to play after [Martínez] but I want to help the team and be like him.

“It was very important to play in Serie A for two years and now I am confident. I made good steps and now I am here to play for the club. I want to enjoy this moment and help the team. I am really looking forward to [playing in] the Champions League but before that I want a first Premier League win to get some momentum.”
Newcastle, meanwhile, concluded a “transformational” transfer window by securing the target that topped their shopping list in May with only hours of the transfer window remaining.

The £51m signing of the Belgium forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo from Lille on deadline day is regarded as a considerable coup and prompted boardroom celebration at the end of a turbulent summer. The 21-year-old is Newcastle’s eighth signing of a transfer window during which Eddie Howe was replaced as manager by Matthias Jaissle and three of the team’s biggest names – Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães – were sold for a total approaching £250m.

Ross Wilson, Newcastle’s sporting director, kept in frequent contact with Fernandez-Pardo’s advisers. “Matias is a strong example of how a transfer window can unfold with twists and turns along the way,” Wilson said. “Back in May he was our top target and we always remained engaged with him. Now at the end of the window he becomes our eighth addition to a refreshed Newcastle United and we are excited to welcome him.”

Fernandez-Pardo’s elusive movement and ability to operate as a No 10, a No 9 or wide-left attacker explains why Newcastle were prepared to stay patient for his signature. “A lot of hours went into this one,” Wilson said. “But we’re clear on our identity and Matias has speed, intensity and work rate in abundance. We believe in his profile a great deal. Our fans will enjoy him and I know he will also enjoy our amazing St James’ Park atmosphere.”

Jaissle seemed equally delighted to have reinforced his frontline with a versatile attacker. “We were all delighted when we knew we could complete this deal,” said the German, who has made three key signings in the £39m Amar Dedic, the £52m Nico González and now Fernandez-Pardo since arriving on Tyneside in early August. “Matias is a highly technical player with explosiveness in his game. He can score and assist, he has courage and the ability to take players on. We’re sure our supporters will enjoy watching him play.”

The Belgian said: “I’m really happy to be here and very proud to be at such a big club. I spoke to the head coach and he really showed me how much he wanted me to be here. In terms of my career progression it made complete sense to come; I didn’t hesitate at all. I can’t wait to start my wonderful adventure here.”
Nick Woltemade’s failure to fit into Jaissle’s high-intensity gameplans explains why the Germany forward, signed for £70m from Stuttgart last August, has joined Juventus on a year-long loan.

Elsewhere, Barcelona have confirmed that Gabriel Jesus has joined from Arsenal on a permanent basis for a fee that is thought to be €10m (£8.6m). The Brazil striker was in attendance for Barcelona’s 5-2 win against Rayo Vallecano on Monday night after a deal was struck over the weekend and he leaves north London as only the 12th player to win the Premier League title with two clubs, having also done so with Manchester City.
Harvey Elliott has also joined Valencia on loan from Liverpool while, across Merseyside, Beto has sealed a £15.5m move from Everton to Fiorentina.
Kevin Danso has joined Sunderland on a year-long loan from Tottenham that should lead to a formal £25m transfer for the Austria centre-half next summer.
Fulham have completed the signing of Manuel Ángel from Real Madrid, having already signed César Palacios and Gonzalo García from the Spanish giants.

bodyEn: Arsenal are running out of time to persuade Julián Álvarez to join them from Atlético Madrid after agreeing to sell Gabriel Martinelli, Gabriel Jesus and Fábio Vieira in deals collectively worth more than £70m.

Álvarez has his heart set on joining Barcelona despite Atlético’s insistence they will not sell to their La Liga rivals – he returned to training on Sunday after being left out of their squad for the win against Sevilla.

Mikel Arteta, the Arsenal manager, is understood to have spoken last week to Álvarez in an effort to persuade the former Manchester City forward to return to the Premier League and to have been informed the Argentina international wants only Barcelona.
Asked directly about Álvarez after victory at Aston Villa on Monday, Arteta replied: “I don’t know. That’s for the people upstairs.”

But Arsenal’s manager did confirm they are seeking reinforcements. “We are trying to improve the squad and until tomorrow night we are going to do that,” he said. “I have been disconnected from the world for 24 hours because I think my energy and focus has to be on the match, but I will get back on it now.”

Barcelona have agreed an £8.6m deal to sign Jesus, who has entered the final year of his contract after falling down the pecking order behind Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyökeres. The 29-year-old Brazilian was at Camp Nou to watch the 5-2 win over Rayo Vallecano on Monday. The Barcelona manager, Hansi Flick, said: “He’s a top striker and of course for us very important, he can give us a lot of things and [I’m] very happy that he’s here.”
However, the Spanish champions would like to sign another attacker after selling Ferran Torres to Paris Saint-Germain and are said to have not given up on Álvarez.

Atlético have agreed a deal with Juventus for Jonathan David on an initial loan with an option to make the Canada forward’s move permanent next summer. But they are understood to be determined to keep Álvarez, who joined from City in 2024.

Arsenal remain hopeful that the 26‑year‑old could change his mind but are believed to be monitoring several other attacking options. Everton’s Iliman Ndiaye was among the players on their shortlist but Manchester City are in advanced talks over a £65m deal for the Senegal forward. Arsenal missed out on Morgan Rogers to Chelsea and failed in an ambitious attempt to sign Vinícius Júnior, the Brazil forward signing a contract extension at Real Madrid.

Arsenal have signed Christos Tzolis to replace Leandro Trossard on the left but Martinelli’s expected departure to Al-Hilal for a club‑record £56m sale would create a space in the squad, although Eberechi Eze is also capable of playing there.

Martinelli, who scored six times in the Champions League last season but only once in the Premier League, was due to have his medical on Monday after being left out of Arsenal’s squad against Coventry on the opening weekend. His fee surpasses the £40m Liverpool paid Arsenal for Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain in 2017.
Vieira looks poised to join Hamburg, where he was on loan last season, for £8.6m.

items.titleZh: 阿森纳同意出售马丁内利和热苏斯后，试图吸引胡利安·阿尔瓦雷斯加盟
items.summaryZh: 阿森纳同意出售马丁内利、热苏斯和维埃拉，总价超7000万镑，但仍努力说服阿尔瓦雷斯加盟。
bodyZh: 阿森纳在同意以总价超过7000万英镑出售加布里埃尔·马丁内利、加布里埃尔·热苏斯和法比奥·维埃拉后，正试图说服胡利安·阿尔瓦雷斯从马德里竞技加盟，但时间所剩无几。
阿尔瓦雷斯一心想要加盟巴塞罗那，尽管马竞坚持不会将球员卖给西甲对手——他在周日回归训练，此前被排除在对阵塞维利亚获胜的大名单之外。
据悉，阿森纳主教练米克尔·阿尔特塔上周与阿尔瓦雷斯进行了交谈，试图说服这位前曼城前锋重返英超，但得到的回复是这位阿根廷国脚只想去巴塞罗那。
在周一客场击败阿斯顿维拉后，阿尔特塔被直接问及阿尔瓦雷斯时回答：“我不知道。这由高层决定。”
但阿森纳主帅确认球队正在寻求补强。“我们正在努力提升阵容，直到明天晚上之前都会这样做，”他说。“我24小时没有与外界联系，因为我觉得自己的精力和注意力必须放在比赛上，但现在我要重新投入到工作中。”
巴塞罗那已同意以860万英镑签下热苏斯，这位29岁的巴西前锋在落后于凯·哈弗茨和维克托·哲凯赖什之后，合同已进入最后一年。他周一在诺坎普观看了5-2战胜巴列卡诺的比赛。巴萨主帅汉斯·弗利克表示：“他是一名顶级前锋，对我们来说当然非常重要，他能给我们带来很多帮助，[我]很高兴他在这里。”
然而，在将费兰·托雷斯出售给巴黎圣日耳曼后，西甲冠军希望再签下一位攻击手，据称他们并未放弃引进阿尔瓦雷斯。
《卫报》的每日足球游戏“On the ball”现已在iOS和Android应用中上线。你能根据线索认出这位英超球星吗？
马德里竞技已与尤文图斯就乔纳森·大卫达成协议，先租借后买断，明年夏天可以选择将这位加拿大前锋的转会永久化。但据悉他们决心留住阿尔瓦雷斯，后者于2024年从曼城加盟。
阿森纳仍希望这位26岁的球员能改变主意，但据信他们正在关注其他几个进攻选项。埃弗顿的伊利曼·恩迪亚耶在他们候选名单上，但曼城正在就这位塞内加尔前锋进行6500万英镑的深入谈判。阿森纳错过了摩根·罗杰斯（切尔西），并在尝试签下维尼修斯·儒尼奥尔时失败，这位巴西边锋与皇马续约。

阿森纳已签下克里斯托斯·佐利斯来替代左路的莱安德罗·特罗萨德，但马丁内利预计将以5600万英镑（俱乐部纪录）转会至利雅得新月，这将为球队腾出一个位置，尽管埃贝雷奇·埃泽也能踢该位置。
马丁内利上赛季在欧冠中打入六球，但英超仅一球入账。他原本预计周一接受体检，此前在首轮对阵考文垂的大名单中被排除。他的转会费超过了2017年利物浦为亚历克斯·张伯伦支付的4000万英镑。
维埃拉看起来将加盟汉堡，他在上赛季被租借至那里，转会费为860万英镑。
